clue.text: Plant rejected a kind of strike after one fellow sacked

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the assembled string is read backwards

parts.note: '-ish' is a suffix meaning roughly or kind of, as in 'greenish'

indicators.note: a fellow who is sacked is thrown out, so that letter goes from the word for a strike

parts.note: to cuff someone is to strike them
F is the abbreviation for fellow; only one of the two Fs is removed

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant looks unwell after a workplace strike in which one worker was fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' drops one F from CUFF to leave CUF; A + ISH + CUF, 'rejected', reads backwards to give the plant. 'kind of strike' looks like a type of industrial action, but 'kind of' is ISH and 'strike' is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a shrub with drooping purple and pink flowers, grown widely in gardens.

clue.text: Fixation with France and French — want to be guillotined!

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
et is the French word for and

indicators.note: a guillotine cuts off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: to want is to wish for

explanation.surface: A French obsession with the guillotine and beheadings.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an abnormal obsession or fixed attachment to something.

clue.text: Virginia entering picked up bow tie at first and a possible alternative

definitions.note: the definition refers back to bow tie in the clue: something worn instead of one

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it
in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: a bow is a curve or arc

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word tie

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A Virginian's choice of neckwear: a bow tie or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'bow tie' from the wordplay: a cravat is neckwear worn in place of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a scarf-like neckband worn by men as a smarter substitute for a tie.

clue.text: Dessert was served as flight attendant was called

indicators.note: food served is set out, so these letters are dished up in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: On a plane, pudding was handed out when the cabin crew member was summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' fits the in-flight meal but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Female cabin crew were once known as air hostesses, a role now termed with a gender-neutral title.

clue.text: Letter on where to drink beer

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the word for beer goes first

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
PH stands for public house, a pub

explanation.surface: A note written on where to get a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first character of the Hebrew alphabet.

clue.text: Current protection scheme in tatters — need extremely qualified expert

indicators.note: read with 'tatters', the phrase 'in tatters' says these letters are torn up and rearranged
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from need

parts.note: an ace is a highly skilled expert

explanation.surface: A grumble that the government's virus protection scheme is falling apart and needs a real expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in tatters' reads as a verdict on the scheme, but it is also the anagram signal with its fodder. Written in 2020, when the UK's Covid contact-tracing programme was widely criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: Test and Trace was the UK government's 2020 programme for testing for Covid and tracking down contacts of the infected.

clue.text: Beat prince — one kept celebrating achievement

indicators.note: a piece kept by another is held inside it

parts.note: to trump is to beat, as in card games
the Roman numeral I is one
Hal is Shakespeare's Prince Hal, the future Henry V

explanation.surface: A victory over royalty, with one person keeping the win.
explanation.walkthrough: Written in 2020: 'Beat' hints at Donald Trump but just means outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphal describes processions or arches that mark and commemorate a victory.

clue.text: Guide leaving town — he knows what's coming

indicators.note: a letter leaving a word departs from it, so it is removed

parts.note: to guide is to steer
T is a standard abbreviation for town

explanation.surface: A tour guide is leaving town, sensing trouble ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer is a prophet, someone able to foretell future events.

clue.text: Drops environmentally unfriendly car India produced

indicators.note: letters produced are made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A polluting vehicle manufactured in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' looks like a verb, but it is the plural noun for falling droplets.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is precipitation polluted by sulphur and nitrogen emissions, damaging forests and lakes.

clue.text: Lives lost in Kansas city — manage to move

indicators.note: in says these pieces are placed inside the name of the city

parts.note: Dodge City is a Wild West town in Kansas
lives means is, as in 'he lives/is in Paris'
L is the abbreviation for lost, as in sports results tables

explanation.surface: A grim Wild West scene: deaths in a Kansas town, and folk managing to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kansas city' looks like Kansas City, Missouri, but it is DODGE, the city name.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to succeed in shifting it from a fixed position.

clue.text: See 5
Widespread infections gathered speed? I'm in charge, initially

indicators.note: letters that are gathered up are collected together and reassembled into a new order
initially points to the opening letters of the words in and charge

explanation.surface: Someone in authority announces that the spread of infections has picked up pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered speed' reads as a stock phrase about acceleration, but 'gathered' is the anagram signal. SPEED and I'M plus I and C ('initially') are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidemics are outbreaks of disease spreading rapidly through a population.

clue.text: Attempt to stay safe at the moment — in support at first

definitions.text: Attempt to stay safe at the moment

indicators.note: at first says the word for support is placed at the front, before the word for in

parts.note: a stay is a prop or support, as in a ship's rigging
to be in is to be at home rather than out

explanation.surface: Pandemic advice: shelter indoors for now, with support given first.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses 'stay' itself, which several solvers disliked. Written during the 2020 lockdowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining indoors was the official instruction for avoiding infection during the 2020 lockdown.

clue.text: Life of Brian not getting an Oscar?

indicators.note: not getting something means going without it, so those letters are dropped from Brian

parts.note: Oscar is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for the letter O

explanation.surface: A film question: did the Monty Python comedy Life of Brian miss out on an Academy Award?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life of Brian' looks like the film title, but 'Life' is the definition and 'of' a link. 'Oscar' looks like the film award but is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or vivacity, the sense in which a lively person is full of life.

clue.text: Heading for Spitalfields, one Ripper suspect's an underworld figure

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order
the heading of a word is its first letter, here of Spitalfields

explanation.surface: Murder in Victorian London's East End: a Jack the Ripper suspect turns out to be a gangland figure.
explanation.walkthrough: S (the head of Spitalfields) with ONE and RIPPER is rearranged. Spitalfields is the East London district of the Ripper murders, and 'underworld figure' sounds like a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Proserpine is the Roman name of Persephone, queen of Hades, a figure of the mythological realm of the dead.

clue.text: 17 accomplished nothing with firm and in government

definitions.note: the answer to 17 down is a female peer's rank, the title held by this person

parts.note: to have accomplished something is to have done or did it
nothing is zero, the letter O
firm means solid or hard

explanation.surface: A peer who achieved little while in business and in government.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido Harding, a Conservative peer, headed England's Covid Test and Trace programme in 2020, which ties her to 5/9.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido Harding sits in the House of Lords as Baroness Harding of Winscombe, so she is a baroness.

clue.text: It's hell! Very angry about country

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: mad means very angry
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: An outburst from someone furious about the state of their country.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is eternal punishment in the afterlife; also used as an exclamation of anger.

clue.text: Getting mates in party at end of day — is money overcoming resistance?

indicators.note: the pieces overcome the letter by surrounding it, taking it within

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: at end of points to the last letter of the word day

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for money, as in economics (M1, M2)

explanation.surface: Is a political party's money winning out at the end of the day as it brings in its friends?
explanation.walkthrough: Pointed at 2020 complaints over contracts to government friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Cronyism is favouritism in appointments, bringing pals into posts of power.

clue.text: Rank boss near useless!

indicators.note: letters that are useless as they stand must be rearranged into something that works

explanation.surface: An insult: the boss is next to useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective meaning foul, but it is the noun for a title in the peerage.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroness is a title in the British peerage, the female equivalent of baron.

clue.text: Rallies, as before, when looks like holding

indicators.note: one word holding another has it inside, so the word for when goes within

parts.note: something that looks like another resembles it
as can mean when, as in 'as I left, it rained'

explanation.surface: Someone's look at a rally that seems a repeat of a past one.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'as' in the definition is not the AS of the wordplay; that comes from 'when'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally troops is to gather them again, and to reassemble is to come together once more.

clue.text: Out of sorts, accused up-and-coming left-winger

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from the bottom, so the letters are reversed
the letters are taken out of the run of words sorts, accused

explanation.surface: An accused person, feeling out of sorts, is a promising young socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro was the communist leader of Cuba, so a left-wing politician.

clue.text: Picked note up in canteen before leaving

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
leaving means these letters go out of the word canteen

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in antenatal

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: soh is the fifth note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: Someone was selected for a job in the canteen just before quitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Chosen means selected, as with a candidate taken from a field.

clue.text: Amorous behaviour not unknown in secluded little spot

indicators.note: not before a letter means that letter is left out of the word for amorous behaviour

parts.note: nooky is British slang for sexual activity
in algebra x, y and z are the unknowns, so Y can stand for an unknown

explanation.surface: Lovemaking that goes unnoticed in a quiet hidden corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small sheltered corner or recess, a spot away from view.

clue.text: Heard cab at rank is a security problem

indicators.note: rank here means foul or gross, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something overheard in a taxi at the cab rank compromises security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' pairs with 'cab' as a taxi stand, but here it means corrupt and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak of stored information to people who should not see it is a serious lapse of security.

clue.text: Obsessive over new record

indicators.note: one word over another is spread over it, enclosing it

parts.note: anal is slang for fussily obsessive

explanation.surface: Someone fussing about a fresh personal best.
explanation.walkthrough: The singular annal is rare; more often seen in the plural for yearly chronicles.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a written account of a single year's events, a historical entry.

clue.text: Queen showing Thatcher animosity? On the contrary

indicators.note: showing means the letters are visible within the words that follow
the surface relation is turned round: the words show the queen, not the queen showing them

explanation.surface: A monarch displaying hostility towards Margaret Thatcher, the British prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says a queen shows animosity; 'On the contrary' turns that round, so the words 'Thatcher animosity' show the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or a raja's wife.

clue.text: Bungling Boris maybe completely lost — it has been said before

definitions.note: a clause, standing for a noun meaning a repetition

indicators.note: something lost goes missing, so those letters are taken from the front

parts.note: Bungling Boris is a phrase whose two words start with the same letter, an example of alliteration
completely means all, as in 'all done'

explanation.surface: A jibe that the bumbling British prime minister of the day is utterly out of his depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bungling Boris' looks like a description of Boris Johnson, but it is an example of alliteration. The definition is a whole clause describing something repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: An iteration is a repetition, a further version of something already done or said.

clue.text: Is it as one originally maintained?

definitions.note: a plural of the letter I, matching a plural answer

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the letters of it and as hold another inside
originally points to the first letter of the word one

explanation.surface: A question asking whether things are as someone first claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the verb opening a question, but it is the plural of the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The iota is the Greek letter equivalent to our I, so several of them are Is.

clue.text: Goal? Fail to score with keeper getting back

parts.note: to miss is to fail to hit the target or score

indicators.note: getting back means returning, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the goalkeeper traditionally wears the number one shirt, written NO I

explanation.surface: A football scene: a goal chance missed, with the goalkeeper scrambling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeper' is the goalkeeper as Number One, written NO I; reversed it gives ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is an aim or task someone sets out to achieve, an objective.

clue.text: Rest have told a story earlier

indicators.note: earlier says the word for told a story comes before the word for have

parts.note: telling a story is a polite way of saying lying, so it means lied
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Someone told a fib earlier and now needs a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told a story' sounds like storytelling but means fibbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline and take a break from activity is to rest.
